items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: This Charlie eventually got to know Mrs. Huston's son...

ctx.x: After Mr. Wade was in our place a certain time, he started making bootleg whiskey. There were barrels of mash in the small room where the man had lived before he moved. He had a copper still that fitted on the gas stove. Mr. Wade started doing good business and I remember that a prohibition officer used to come there at times and drink with Mr. Wade. I used to taste the alcohol when it was hot and dripping from the still.

Then Mr. Wade made the acquaintance of a fellow by the name of Charlie who used to peddle his whiskey. This Charlie eventually got to know Mrs. Huston's son and one Sunday they were out drinking somewhere and Charlie persuaded the boy to sell him his pistol for 12 dollars. As Charlie was pretty tipsy, Mrs. Huston's son didn't trust him too much and took the bullets out of the pistol before he agreed to sell it to Charlie. Mrs. Huston's son was a real country fellow and Charlie eventually confidenced this guy into…

Then Charlie went out on the street and two white men were coming along. They happened to be detectives and Charlie must have recognised them as such because he pulled out his pistol and started shooting at them. They kept coming towards him and pulled their guns also. Charlie turned and ran and the detectives took after him and finally cornered him in a lumber yard, disarmed him and took him to jail.
